correctness.rationale: For a vertex outside F in part i, the exact neighbor count into F is |F|-|F∩V_i|. This gives a necessary-and-sufficient fort criterion. The proof exhausts minimal forts by size: all valid pairs are classified, triple transversals are characterized, and every fort of size at least four contains one of those smaller forts. The count follows from disjoint cases. Exhaustive direct neighborhood checks through order 9 match the theorem.

value.rationale: The fort hypergraph is a standard obstruction object for zero forcing and underlies transversal, matching, fractional, and compatible-fort methods. Complete multipartite graphs are a canonical graph family. The theorem gives the full minimal-obstruction hypergraph, shows a sharp structural transition from the known 2-uniform biclique case to rank 3, and supplies an exact enumerator usable in subsequent fort-based optimization or compatibility questions.
